figures.title: Shared prefix blocks are reused and kept alive by refcount
figures.caption: A's prefill builds the system-prompt blocks S1 and S2 with refcount 1. B's lookup matches both, raises them to 2, and prefills only its own suffix. When A finishes, S1 and S2 drop to 1 and U_A becomes evictable; only when B finishes do the shared blocks reach 0. Block-level refcounts keep the prefix alive across the gap between the two requests.
figures.alt: A four-column timeline: A arrives, B arrives, A finishes, B finishes. The shared-prefix lane is built at A's arrival, reused at B's arrival, held when A finishes, and empty when B finishes. The suffix lane builds U_A, builds U_B, frees U_A, and frees U_B. The refcount lane reads 1, 2, 1, 0 for the shared blocks.

data.note: A request-level LRU would evict S1 and S2 when A finishes and destroy the prefix B is still using; block-level LRU with refcounts keeps them until both requests are done.

anim.intro: Follow two requests through one shared system prompt.

steps.label: A's prefill computes the system-prompt blocks S1 and S2; each has refcount 1.
B's lookup matches S1 and S2, raises both to refcount 2, and prefills only its suffix.
A finishes: S1 and S2 drop to 1 and U_A becomes an eviction candidate.
B finishes: the shared blocks drop to 0 and can be evicted.

figures.title: Two lookup structures that bind a block to its exact prefix
figures.caption: A block is reusable only if every token before it matches. vLLM chains hashes, folding the previous block's hash into the next so the same tokens after a different prefix hash differently. SGLang walks a radix tree, splitting an edge where tokens diverge; both reuse whole blocks only.
figures.alt: Two aligned panels. The chained-hash panel defines h1 as the hash of S1's tokens plus the namespace and h2 as the hash of S2's tokens plus h1, and notes that identical tokens after a different prefix produce a different h2. The radix-tree panel shows a root, an edge for S1, a node, an edge for S2, and the rule that an edge splits where tokens diverge; only full blocks are reused and a partial tail is recomputed.

panels.title: Chained block hash
items: same tokens after a different prefix hash differently
panels.note: Namespace: weights, tokenizer, adapter, dtype, block size, and starting position. Two requests share a block only if the whole chain matches.

panels.title: Radix-tree walk
items: root to edge S1 to node to edge S2
split the edge where tokens diverge
reuse full blocks only; a partial tail is recomputed
panels.note: Divergence inside a block recomputes the whole block, so block size trades lookup metadata against recomputation; 16 is the common default.

figures.title: Token-level hit rate is the one that tracks prefill work
figures.caption: In the worked example 90 of 110 prompt tokens are cached, a token-level rate of 81.8 percent, while only 1 of 2 requests hits, 50 percent. A request with one cached token counts as a request-level hit but saves almost no compute, which is why the token-level rate is the one that tracks prefill work.
figures.alt: Two horizontal bars. The token-level hit rate is 81.8 percent, 90 of 110 tokens. The request-level hit rate is 50 percent, 1 of 2 requests.

data.note: The counters are per prompt token: increment the query counter for every token considered for matching and the hit counter for every reused KV block. Request-level counts a request as a hit even when one token matched.
